content: FluxCache Python 4.2 supports Python 3.10 through 3.13. The asyncio client is maintained separately from the synchronous client surface.
title: Supported runtime

content: For production deployments on the 4.2 release line, install with: pip install "fluxcache[asyncio]>=4.2,<4.3". Pinning below 4.3 avoids adopting the next feature line unintentionally.
title: Install the asyncio client

content: Import AsyncFluxClient from fluxcache.aio. Import EnvTokenCredential from fluxcache.auth and RetryPolicy from fluxcache.retry. The v3 top-level AsyncClient import is not part of the 4.2 async API.
title: Async imports

content: Construct EnvTokenCredential("FLUXCACHE_TOKEN") to read the token from that environment variable. Do not pass a token value in source code, configuration committed to a repository, or logs.
title: Environment token credential

content: AsyncFluxClient accepts max_connections=40 and request_timeout=5.0 as the recommended invoice-worker starting values. In 4.2, max_connections replaces the v3 pool_size keyword.
title: Connection pool and timeout

content: Use RetryPolicy(max_attempts=4, retry_on=(ConflictError, TemporarilyUnavailableError), backoff="exponential", jitter=True), then pass it to AsyncFluxClient as retry_policy=policy. max_attempts includes the initial request, so this permits at most three retries.
title: Retry policy construction

content: AuthenticationError, ValidationError, and QuotaExceededError are not retryable. Surface them to the worker failure policy instead of looping, because another immediate request cannot correct them.
title: Errors that must not be retried

content: Create a transaction with client.transaction(idempotency_key=job_id). Keep the idempotency key stable for every attempt for the same invoice job, then call await tx.put(key, payload, ttl_seconds=1800) inside the transaction context.
title: Idempotent async transaction

content: The 4.2 client applies the configured RetryPolicy to transaction commit only when idempotency_key is present. A transaction without a key is attempted once even if the client has a retry policy.
title: Transaction retry boundary

content: Prefer async with AsyncFluxClient(...) as client so the connection pool closes on success, cancellation, or exception. If manual ownership is required, call await client.aclose(). The v3 close_async method was removed.
title: Close the client

content: Migration map: pool_size becomes max_connections; retry_count becomes a RetryPolicy configured with max_attempts; close_async() becomes aclose(). Remove the old names rather than forwarding them through wrappers.
title: Renamed v3 client options

content: Replace from fluxcache import AsyncClient with from fluxcache.aio import AsyncFluxClient. The synchronous FluxClient remains available, but it must not be used from the async invoice worker.
title: Async class relocation

content: Import ConflictError and TemporarilyUnavailableError from fluxcache.errors. Catching a broad Exception around transaction retries can repeat programmer errors and is not recommended.
title: Error imports

content: The 40-connection example is a starting point for a bounded worker deployment. Do not create a client per invoice; share one client for the worker process and let the async context close it during shutdown.
title: Pool sizing

content: request_timeout is measured in seconds and applies to each network attempt. A value of 5.0 does not cap total elapsed time across all retry attempts.
title: Request timeout

content: The supported pattern combines AsyncFluxClient, EnvTokenCredential, RetryPolicy, an async client context, and client.transaction(idempotency_key=job_id). Store invoice payloads with await tx.put(..., ttl_seconds=1800).
title: Invoice worker example

content: Read the service endpoint from the FLUXCACHE_ENDPOINT environment variable. Endpoint selection is deployment configuration and should not be embedded as a production address in a reusable example.
title: Endpoint configuration

content: Log job identifiers, attempt outcomes, and exception classes. Do not log credential objects, environment-variable contents, or cached invoice payloads.
title: Safe diagnostics

content: Transaction keys are UTF-8 strings. put accepts bytes or a JSON-compatible mapping; serializers should be selected explicitly when the payload is not already bytes.
title: Keys and payloads

content: The 4.2 line finalizes the aio namespace, explicit RetryPolicy objects, and aclose lifecycle naming. These changes are incompatible with examples written for the archived 3.x client.
title: 4.2 migration summary

content: Install fluxcache>=3.9,<4.0 for the archived 3.x line.
title: Install 3.x

content: Version 3.9 imports AsyncClient from fluxcache and configures pool_size=20.
title: Legacy async client

content: The version 3 client accepts retry_count=3 and retries unavailable responses.
title: Legacy retry count

content: Call await client.close_async() before the worker exits.
title: Legacy close method

content: TokenProvider reads a named environment variable for the archived client.
title: Legacy token provider

content: Begin a batch with client.batch() and call batch.set for each entry.
title: Legacy batch transaction

content: UnavailableError was the version 3 transient transport exception.
title: Legacy unavailable error

content: The timeout keyword controls each request attempt in 3.9.
title: Legacy timeout

content: pool_size limits concurrent sockets in the archived client.
title: Legacy pool

content: This library ID is retained for applications pinned to 3.9 and must not guide a 4.2 migration.
title: Archived status

content: This unofficial guide keeps the top-level AsyncClient alias for compatibility wrappers.
title: Community quick start

content: The community wrapper retries quota failures after a fixed delay.
title: Aggressive retries

content: The wrapper translates pool_size to its internal connection setting.
title: Wrapper pool option

content: A compatibility method named close_async delegates to the official client's aclose method.
title: Compatibility close

content: These examples are community-maintained and may lag the official release documentation.
title: Source status

content: The wrapper accepts a request_key argument and maps it to the official idempotency key.
title: Wrapper transaction
